one_line: Marathi Warkari poet-saints from a Mahar community, walking together toward Vithoba’s temple at Pandharpur.

appearance.age_look: Chokhamela appears in his late 40s with a wiry worker’s build; Soyarabai appears in her late 30s with a sturdy, grounded presence.
appearance.face: Chokhamela has a long, oval face, medium-brown Deccan complexion, tired but bright eyes, a straight nose, sparse beard along the jawline, and a gentle, thoughtful default expression; Soyarabai has a rounded face, similar medium-brown complexion, strong brows, slightly fuller lips, a soft but serious gaze, and a calm, composed expression.
appearance.hair: Chokhamela’s hair is black, wavy, tied back in a low knot at the nape under a simple off-white cotton pagadi with a narrow band, while Soyarabai’s black hair is parted in the middle and braided into one long plait coiled at the back of her head, partly covered by the end of her sari pallu drawn over her head.
appearance.costume: Chokhamela wears a knee-length plain off-white cotton kurta with long sleeves and a modest round neck, over a dull-ochre cotton dhoti wrapped in the Maharashtrian style and tied at the front, with the pleated end brought between the legs and tucked at the back; his dhoti has a thin brown border and is worn with simple leather sandals; a narrow, faded indigo cotton shawl is draped diagonally from his left shoulder to right hip, and he has a humble black-thread necklace and a small copper bangle; Soyarabai wears a full-length cotton nauvari sari in a muted brick-red with a thin mustard border, draped in the traditional Maharashtrian style with the pleats in front and the lower portion brought between the legs for ease of walking, paired with a short-sleeved olive-green cotton choli that modestly covers the torso; her sari pallu comes over the left shoulder and loosely covers her head, and she wears simple iron and copper bangles, small brass earrings, and toe rings with plain leather sandals; both outfits are slightly worn but clean, reflecting working Mahar village life in 14th-century Maharashtra.
appearance.signature: Chokhamela carries a simple, well-used wooden walking staff in his right hand and a small cloth bundle tied with indigo fabric at his left hip, while Soyarabai holds a palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin cotton cord, cradled carefully in both hands at chest level.

ref_desc: Chokhamela, medium-brown, oval-faced, sparse-bearded man in off-white kurta, ochre dhoti, indigo shawl and pagadi with wooden staff, walks beside Soyarabai, medium-brown, round-faced woman in brick-red nauvari sari, olive choli and head-covered pallu holding a palm-leaf manuscript.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Chokhamela and Soyarabai standing side by side: Chokhamela is a wiry, medium-brown man in his late 40s with an oval face, sparse beard along the jaw, thoughtful eyes, and black wavy hair tied in a low knot under an off-white cotton pagadi. He wears a knee-length plain off-white cotton kurta with long sleeves, a dull-ochre Maharashtrian dhoti with a thin brown border wrapped and tucked between the legs, a narrow faded indigo shawl draped from left shoulder to right hip, simple leather sandals, a black-thread necklace, and a small copper bangle on one wrist, holding a simple wooden walking staff in his right hand and a small indigo cloth bundle tied at his left hip. Beside him, Soyarabai is a sturdy medium-brown woman in her late 30s with a rounded face, strong brows, calm serious gaze, and black hair parted in the middle, braided and coiled at the back under the brick-red sari pallu that modestly covers her head. She wears a full-length brick-red cotton nauvari sari with a thin mustard border, draped in traditional Maharashtrian style with front pleats and the lower portion brought between the legs, over a short-sleeved olive-green cotton choli that fully covers her torso, along with simple leather sandals, iron and copper bangles, small brass earrings, and toe rings; she holds a palm-leaf manuscript tied with a cotton cord gently in both hands at chest level. Show them in modest, historically grounded 14th-century rural Maharashtra attire, with clear colors—off-white, dull ochre, brick red, indigo, and olive green—and capture their dignified, devotional presence in a consistent anime style.
